dataset.name: Water level data collected in the Rifle Floodplain, Colorado, USA
description: This package contains water level data from 28 instrumented wells at the Old Rifle field site, located in Colorado. This data was collected at the LBNL Rifle site for the DOE funded LBNL SFA project and its predecessor project the Rifle IFRC . The name of each file corresponds to the name of the well in the well field. The names of these wells and locations are given in the file boreholes_rifle.csv. Each file contains data on the timestamp, water level, and QA indicator. There is more detailed information in the README file, including the two possible reasons why some data points are marked as invalid.

spatialCoverage.description: Site: Rifle, Colorado US-RIF. The Rifle site is located in the east side of the Upper Colorado River Basin (UCRB) in northwestern Colorado. The site had a former uranium and vanadium mill, which operated between 1924 and 1958. As a uranium‐contaminated site it has been the focus of several intense hydrological, biogeochemical, and bioremediation research activities., and was used by the DOE Sustainable Systems Scientific Focus Area to explore how climate drivers influence hydrological processes and biogeochemical cycling within the Colorado River Basin. The Rifle site is located atop a floodplain adjacent to the Colorado River floodplain systems within the UCRB, and is representative of floodplains in the UCRB based upon its overall aquifer properties and hydrological coupling to the Colorado River.

measurementTechnique:
This water level data was calculated from vented pressure transducers which were deployed in these wells. Data was recorded at 5 to 15 min intervals and transmitted to a central server using the DOE LM SOARS system from where it was transmitted to a LBNL Data management system. Start and end date of instrumentation varies by wells.The transducers record a pressure which is translated to a water height above the transducer. This water height is converted to a absolute water height (given in the NAVD88 datum). This is done by using the Top of Casing (TOC) of each well (which was measured in NAVD88) and the depth to transducer, and then converting the measured water height above the transducer to an absolute water level using the
following formula
Absolute water level = TOC - depth_to_transducer+ waterheight_above_sensor
The data provided here is the corrected data.
